meta.paper_title: Aligning Machine and Human Visual Representations

dimension_1_data_split_hygiene.justification: Splits are explicitly defined in code and honored, not merely asserted. code/data_utils.py:84-97 maps train=trainset.txt, heldout=testset1.txt, test2=testset2.txt/testset2_repeat.txt. The teacher head (M1) is fit on THINGS train triplets (train_subsample=300000, config in runs/M1_teacher_fit/eval_heldout.json) and evaluated on the disjoint testset1 heldout (n_triplets_heldout=15640). The student alignment finetune (M3/M5) is trained on ImageNet-val images (runs/M3_aligned_dinov2/train_summary.json), which is entirely disjoint from the THINGS triplet evaluation used for C2a/C2b/C3, so the reported THINGS Spearman/accuracy gains are on held-out data w.r.t. student training. The 'human similarity' ground truth for the Spearman metric is built from THINGS *train* triplets (code/eval_student_similarity.py:224-235 build_human_similarity_from_triplets(load_triplets('train'))) and correlated against the model's own features on the eval concept set — this is a label construction (a fixed human-derived similarity prior), not model fitting, so it introduces no train/test leakage. C3's two-worker uncertainty split (testset2 vs testset2_repeat) is separate from the M1/M3 fit and eval splits. Downstream 1-shot (M7/M8) uses 1 train-exemplar-per-class + disjoint test items (raw_per_student_per_dataset in runs/M7_downstream/results.json, n_train_per_class=1). No fit-then-score-on-same-split path was found. EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:27-30 documents the disjointness. Clean.

dimension_2_label_validity.justification: The primary ground truth is the THINGS human triplet odd-one-out judgments — the canonical, externally-sourced, human-generated similarity label used by the paper itself; it is non-circular (generated by human participants, independent of the models under test) and directly operationalizes 'human similarity structure' for C1a, C2, and the choice/RSA components of C3 (runs/M1_teacher_fit/eval_heldout.json, runs/M3_aligned_dinov2/eval_things_multilevel.json, runs/M6_behavioural/results.json). However, two secondary labels have documented validity gaps. (1) C1b's hierarchical 'correctness' is a synthetic proxy: the odd-one-out at each level is defined by the same WordNet/BREEDS-derived hierarchy that constructed the triplets — the run's own audit (verify/C1b_teacher_hierarchy_monotonic/main_experiment_audit/EXPERIMENT_AUDIT.md, Check A) flags this as 'essentially circular ... verifying that the hierarchy construction is self-consistent', with no human ground truth. (2) C3's uncertainty label is per-triplet two-worker agreement on testset2/testset2_repeat (runs/M6_behavioural/results.json, human_agreement_rate=0.863), a sparse binary proxy that substitutes for the paper's continuous human response-time uncertainty signal (paper Sec 2.1, coarse rho=0.479-0.506) — an under-validated proxy honestly caveated in claims_ledger.json C3 caveats. The gold THINGS label for the headline claims is excellent; the two secondary proxies (one circular, one sparse) are real, disclosed gaps.

dimension_3_resource_fidelity.justification: The task.md experiment-stage resources are honored exactly in the main experiment: student = DINOv2 ViT-B (facebook/dinov2-base; M4 config student_ckpt=/data/zhenqian/models/dinov2-base, n_train_params_M=86.58 in runs/M3_aligned_dinov2/train_summary.json), teacher = SigLIP-So400m (google/siglip-so400m-patch14-384, held fixed per EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:162), evaluation dataset = THINGS (15,640 held-out triplets). Deviations are disclosed, not silent: (a) ImageNet finetune pool substituted ImageNet-val 50k (40k sampled, seed 42) for the plan's ImageNet-train 150k because only val is on disk (EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:18,20; claims_ledger.json open_items) — justified since the KD alignment loss is unsupervised (class labels unused), but it is both a source swap (val vs train) and a ~73% data-size reduction that may shift absolute Spearman levels. (b) M7 downstream datasets (Birds/UC-Merced/Colon/Aircraft) and M8 OOD panel (BREEDS entity13/living17/non-living26/entity30 + ImageNet-A) were substituted with on-disk analogs (DTD, Fashion-MNIST, ImageNet-val slices, BREEDS super13/26) — these datasets are listed under task.md's *verify-stage candidate* pool ('use as needed'), so the substitution is in more-lenient territory, and it is explicitly disclosed and even drove the C4a->C4a_v2 / C4b->C4b_v2 rewrites. The core model/dataset the user asked to test is used exactly; the deviations are documented and reasoned. Minor deduction for the ImageNet val-vs-train + size subset in the main pipeline.

dimension_4_evidence_sufficiency.justification: used_n is large and matches claim strength for every headline claim. C1a: 15,640 held-out THINGS triplets (runs/M1_teacher_fit/eval_heldout.json). C2a/C2b: 15,640 eval triplets + 1,714,022 Spearman pairs (runs/M3_aligned_dinov2/eval_things_multilevel.json, spearman_n_pairs=1714022). C2c control on the matched 40k finetune. C3: 36,187 usable triplets (runs/M6_behavioural/results.json). M7: 14,380 test items; M8: 17,704 test items. Finetune scale 40k images (EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:20). All far exceed the run's stated floors (EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:27-30). The only thin spot is the C2b fine level (n_triplets_fine=33, n_pairs_fine=0 in the eval JSON), and this is NOT overclaimed — it is explicitly reported as inconclusive ('n too small to conclude either way', spearman_fine=NaN) rather than asserted. Claim strength is calibrated to evidence with caveats attached (claims_ledger.json C2b, C3). No conclusion is stated without the corresponding experiment having been run.

dimension_5_statistical_rigor.justification: Uncertainty is reported throughout: bootstrap CI95 on every triplet-accuracy and per-level metric (e.g. teacher 0.590 [0.582,0.598] vs unaligned 0.460 [0.452,0.467], non-overlapping, in runs/M1_teacher_fit/eval_heldout.json; M3 0.5637 [0.556,0.571] vs M4 0.431 [0.423,0.438]), and paired-bootstrap significance (p_positive, diff CI95) on all downstream/OOD deltas (runs/M7_downstream/results.json, runs/M8_ood/results.json show p_positive=0.00 or 1.00 with tight diff CIs). Claimed differences (Delta_rho=+0.366, 7.3x threshold; +15.2pp choice; +20pp BREEDS) vastly exceed the reported noise. A one-axis robustness check exists (verify model-swap DINOv2 ViT-B->ViT-S reproduces Delta_rho=+0.324, runs/verify/C2a_model_swap_dinov2_vits/). The gap: all training runs use a single seed (seed=42 everywhere) — the reported CIs are resampling uncertainty of a single trained checkpoint, so robustness to *training* randomness (re-init / data-order) is unverified; no multi-seed variance is reported. Given large effects + genuine resampling CIs + significance testing + one cross-architecture confirmation, but single training seed, this sits just below the multi-seed anchor.

dimension_6_causal_claim_validity.justification: The improvement claims are causal ('distilling ... improves ...') and are supported by a genuine intervention rather than correlation: the alignment finetune itself is the manipulation, and the run compares the intervened student (M3 aligned) against the un-intervened baseline (M4 unaligned) on identical held-out data. Critically, it includes the correct specificity control for this mechanism — C2c/M5 is a matched-cost, matched-schedule finetune that swaps only the teacher (unaligned SigLIP soft-labels, no THINGS-fit head), isolating the human-alignment component: M3-M4=+0.366 vs M5-M4=+0.085, so 77% of the Spearman gain is attributable specifically to human alignment and rules out generic KD label-smoothing (runs/M5_control_dinov2/eval_things_multilevel.json, EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:98-107). A coefficient/scope sweep exists (iterations swept alpha in {1.0,0.1} and scope in {full, LoRA}; review-stage/AUTO_ITERATION_FINAL_REPORT.md Appendix), and a cross-model swap (ViT-S) confirms direction. Wording matches the intervention-based evidence. The main missing rigor element is a random-direction/placebo teacher baseline beyond the single matched control, but the matched-cost non-aligned control is the appropriate placebo here.

dimension_7_result_provenance.justification: Most headline numbers trace exactly to on-disk products and agree with them: C1a teacher_triplet_accuracy=0.5901 (runs/M1_teacher_fit/eval_heldout.json) = ledger 0.590; C2a spearman_aggregate aligned=0.555385 / unaligned=0.189119 (runs/M3|M4_.../eval_things_multilevel.json) = report/ledger 0.555/0.189 and Delta=+0.366; C2c M5=0.2736 (runs/M5_control_dinov2/eval_things_multilevel.json); C3 choice 0.5857/0.4338, uncertainty 0.0545/0.0168, RSA 0.5554/0.1891 (runs/M6_behavioural/results.json); all M7/M8 deltas match runs/M7_downstream/results.json and runs/M8_ood/results.json exactly. Two provenance defects: (1) MATERIAL — C1b: EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:57-59 and claims_ledger.json cite coarse=0.750, mid=0.747, fine=0.817 [0.794,0.840], but the on-disk product runs/M2_hierarchical_pseudo/level_separation.json (and log.txt) shows coarse=0.737, mid=0.809, fine=n=0/agreement_rate=NaN. The reported fine=0.817 has NO on-disk backing and directly contradicts the product's n=0; coarse/mid are also mismatched. The run's own audit caught this (verify/C1b.../EXPERIMENT_AUDIT.md Check C: 'fine level shows n=0 in JSON but 0.817 in prose'). (2) MINOR — M3 triplet accuracy is reported as 0.556 [0.548,0.564] (EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:76) but the on-disk JSON has 0.5637 [0.556,0.571]. The headline claims are all grounded in real execution and traceable, but C1b's reported per-level numbers are contradicted by their own product — an isolated back-fill/stale-citation on a secondary claim, self-disclosed.

dimension_8_cross_artifact_consistency.justification: Verdicts and integrity states are propagated consistently across artifacts — C2a is PASS everywhere (VERIFY_REPORT.md, INTEGRITY_AUDIT.md, claims_ledger.json); the WARN claims (C1b, C2b, C4a, C4b) are uniformly flagged WARN/conditional across the integrity audit, verify report, and ledger, and no claim is PASS-in-one-artifact-yet-broken-in-another. However there are several numeric inconsistencies revealing loose bookkeeping. (1) MATERIAL prose-vs-product contradiction on C1b: report/ledger fine=0.817, coarse=0.750, mid=0.747 vs on-disk level_separation.json coarse=0.737, mid=0.809, fine=NaN(n=0) — a prose conclusion citing a number its own product does not contain. (2) M3 triplet accuracy 0.556 (EXPERIMENT_RESULTS.md:76) vs 0.5637 (eval_things_multilevel.json). (3) Per-level Spearman is computed on inconsistent pair sets between the two arms: M3 coarse n_pairs_coarse=183 / mid=1194 but M4 coarse n_pairs_coarse=13861 / mid=328455 (different code versions of the pair-construction), so the C2b per-level Delta_rho (+0.526 coarse, +0.427 mid) is not a clean paired comparison. None of these overturns the headline C2a/C3 verdicts, and the integrity gate self-flags the C1b/C2b issues (mitigating), but the count and one material prose-vs-number contradiction place this below the 'one minor inconsistency' adequate anchor.

C1.claim: A teacher model fitted to human triplet-similarity judgments on THINGS captures human similarity structure well enough that, when applied to a large unlabelled image corpus (ImageNet), it can synthesise a large body of human-like similarity judgments spanning multiple abstraction levels.

method.justification: 9a: The method matches the paper's teacher-construction category: a frozen SigLIP-So400m image tower with a triplet-KL alignment head fit on THINGS train triplets, then applied to ImageNet to synthesize hierarchical triplets (M1 in code/fit_teacher_head.py, M2 in code/eval_hierarchical_triplets.py). This correctly targets 'fit a surrogate human-similarity teacher on THINGS and use it to generate multi-level judgments on ImageNet'. Minor deviations from the paper: a small MLP head rather than the paper's affine transform + uncertainty distillation, and WordNet/BREEDS-hierarchy triplet synthesis rather than the paper's teacher-representation clustering-based sampling. The method family is suitable for the claim.

experiment.justification: 9b: C1a is well-designed — held-out THINGS triplet accuracy vs both the unaligned SigLIP baseline and the 1/3 chance floor, with bootstrap CI95 (runs/M1_teacher_fit/eval_heldout.json). C1b is weaker: (i) the per-level 'correctness' is defined by the same hierarchy that built the triplets (circular self-consistency, flagged in verify/C1b.../EXPERIMENT_AUDIT.md Check A); (ii) the fine level yielded n=0 usable triplets on disk (level_separation.json), so the 'spanning multiple abstraction levels' at fine grain is untested; (iii) the pre-declared monotonic ordering was not met (fine>coarse), honestly reported. The C1a design is strong; the C1b hierarchy experiment has a circularity gap and a construction failure at the fine level.

result.justification: 9c: The core of C1 reproduces well qualitatively — the fit teacher reaches 0.590 held-out THINGS triplet accuracy (runs/M1_teacher_fit/eval_heldout.json), close to the paper's reported 61.7% and well above the unaligned SigLIP (0.460) and chance (0.333), confirming the teacher captures human similarity structure. The 'multiple abstraction levels' generation is partially supported: on-disk coarse (0.737) and mid (0.809) beat chance, agreeing with the paper's direction. But the reported fine-level result (0.817) has no on-disk support (level_separation.json fine n=0/NaN) — the specific number contradicts its product — and the pre-declared monotonic ordering fails. Direction agrees with the paper for C1a and coarse/mid, but one sub-result (fine) is unsupported/contradicted and the reported numbers mismatch the product.

C2.claim: Distilling this human-like similarity structure into pretrained vision foundation models (DINOv2, supervised ViT-L, contrastive image–text models) via a dedicated alignment loss substantially improves their Spearman correlation with human similarity judgments at multiple abstraction levels.

method.justification: 9a: The method matches the paper: full-backbone KL-divergence distillation (triplet_kl loss, alpha=1.0) of DINOv2 ViT-B against the THINGS-fit teacher on the ImageNet pool, then held-out THINGS Spearman vs the unaligned baseline (code/align_student.py, code/eval_student_similarity.py, runs/M3_aligned_dinov2/train_summary.json). This is the paper's 'similarity-space distillation via KL objective' category and is exactly the right mechanism for testing whether distillation improves human-similarity correlation. A matched-cost specificity control (M5) plus a coefficient/scope sweep add rigor. Only DINOv2 ViT-B (the task's specified experiment-stage student) is the main; the paper's ViT-L / contrastive students are covered only by one verify swap (ViT-S).

experiment.justification: 9b: Design is strong — aligned (M3) vs unaligned (M4) on identical held-out THINGS, aggregate + per-level Spearman + triplet accuracy with bootstrap CIs, a matched-cost non-aligned control (C2c), and a cross-architecture verify swap (ViT-S, robustness=1.00). The metric (Spearman rank correlation with human triplet-derived similarity) corresponds strictly to the claim. Weaknesses: the per-level (C2b) Spearman is computed on inconsistent pair sets between the two arms (M3 coarse=183 pairs vs M4 coarse=13861 pairs; eval JSONs), and the fine level has 0 usable pairs, so the 'multiple abstraction levels' facet is only solidly demonstrated at coarse+mid; single training seed. Main aggregate design is sound and criteria were pre-set (Delta_rho>=0.05), not post-hoc.

result.justification: 9c: Strong qualitative agreement with the paper. Aggregate Spearman rises from 0.189 (unaligned) to 0.555 (aligned), Delta_rho=+0.366 = 7.3x the pre-set threshold with non-overlapping CI95 (runs/M3_aligned_dinov2/eval_things_multilevel.json), and this direction/magnitude is confirmed under the ViT-S swap (Delta_rho=+0.324) and holds across alpha=0.1 and LoRA regimes (AUTO_ITERATION_FINAL_REPORT.md Appendix: +0.373, +0.335). C2c shows 77% of the gain is human-alignment-specific. Per-level: coarse Delta_rho=+0.526, mid +0.427 (large positive, agreeing with the paper's multi-level improvement); fine inconclusive and honestly flagged. This is exactly the paper's central finding (substantial multi-level human-alignment improvement) reproduced with a large, verified effect.

C3.claim: After alignment, the fine-tuned student models more accurately reproduce human behavioural patterns and uncertainty on similarity tasks than their unaligned counterparts.

method.justification: 9a: The method broadly fits — forward-only behavioural + uncertainty comparison of aligned (M3) vs unaligned (M4): per-triplet choice-agreement on the human-consensus subset, model-confidence-vs-human-agreement rank correlation, model->human KL, and RSA between model and human RDMs (code/eval_behavioural_uncertainty.py, runs/M6_behavioural/results.json). Choice-agreement and RSA are apt operationalizations. The uncertainty sub-method deviates from the paper: the paper uses continuous human response times as the uncertainty proxy, whereas here uncertainty is per-triplet two-worker agreement (a binary/sparse proxy), because RT data was unavailable. Reasonable but a weaker proxy for the uncertainty facet.

experiment.justification: 9b: The design is reasonable and large-scale (n=36,187 usable triplets, two-worker agreement rate 0.863; runs/M6_behavioural/results.json), with three conjunctive predicates (choice / uncertainty / RSA) each requiring aligned>unaligned in the predicted direction, pre-declared. The choice (+15.2pp) and RSA (0.555 vs 0.189) metrics are robust. The uncertainty metric is the weak facet: the two-worker binary agreement label is a sparse signal, yielding near-floor Spearman (0.054 vs 0.017), so the uncertainty predicate is met only weakly and cannot strongly distinguish signal from noise. Single seed, no error bars on the uncertainty Spearman. Honest but the uncertainty facet is under-powered relative to the claim.

result.justification: 9c: Behaviour and RSA reproduce the paper strongly and directionally: aligned choice-accuracy-on-agreed 0.586 vs 0.434 (+15.2pp) and RSA Spearman 0.555 vs 0.189 (+0.366), plus lower human->model KL (0.228 vs 0.271), all agreeing with the paper's finding that aligned models better reproduce human behaviour (runs/M6_behavioural/results.json). The uncertainty sub-result agrees only in direction but is far weaker than the paper (0.054 vs 0.017 here, vs the paper's coarse rho=0.479-0.506) — this deviation is disclosed and attributed to the sparse two-worker proxy and lack of RT data (claims_ledger.json C3 caveat). One sub-result (uncertainty) deviates in magnitude with the reason disclosed; the behavioural/RSA core agrees.

C4.claim: Alignment is not at odds with utility: aligned student models match or exceed the originals on diverse downstream tasks and improve out-of-distribution robustness.

method.justification: 9a: The method category is appropriate: 1-shot cosine/linear-probe top-1 on downstream classification (M7) and protocol-standard top-1 per split for OOD (M8), aligned vs unaligned, with paired-bootstrap (code/eval_downstream.py, runs/M7_downstream/results.json, runs/M8_ood/results.json) — this mirrors the paper's linear-probe 1-shot + BREEDS + ImageNet-A evaluation. The method itself is suited to the utility/OOD claim. The main method caveat is that the aligned checkpoint is produced by a simplified/aggressive KD recipe (alpha=1.0 full-backbone, 40k ImageNet-val, no clustering-based soft-labels) rather than the paper's full AligNet recipe, which conditions what the downstream test is actually measuring.

experiment.justification: 9b: The design has real strengths — paired-bootstrap significance on every dataset/split, and, importantly, genuine hyperparameter exploration to distinguish a true negative from under-exploration: iterations swept alpha in {1.0, 0.1} and adaptation scope in {full, LoRA r=16}, with code-bug fixes to the LoRA eval path (AUTO_ITERATION_FINAL_REPORT.md 4b.1-4b.2). Weaknesses: (i) dataset substitution — the plan's Birds/UC-Merced/Colon/Aircraft and BREEDS entity13/living17/non-living26/entity30 + ImageNet-A were not tested; on-disk analogs were used and 3/5 OOD substitute splits are not genuine OOD (INTEGRITY_AUDIT.md C4b WARN); (ii) the reproduction did not implement the paper's full AligNet distillation recipe, so a utility loss may partly reflect recipe under-fidelity rather than a property of AligNet — the alpha/LoRA sweep probes loss-weight and scope but not the full recipe. Metric (top-1) is reasonable; criteria were not relaxed to force a pass (C4a honestly reported not-established). Honest but partially under-faithful and on a substitute panel.

result.justification: 9c: The reproduction DISAGREES with the paper on utility and reports it honestly rather than disguising it: aligned is strictly worse on all 4 downstream 1-shot substitutes (mean Delta=-0.284, p_positive=0.00 each; runs/M7_downstream/results.json) — the opposite of the paper's 'match or exceed'. The universal-quantifier claims were explicitly retracted/narrowed (C4a->C4a_v2 documented trade-off; C4b->C4b_v2 selective-BREEDS-only) with no goalpost-tuning to force agreement. Partial agreement with the paper's OOD story does hold: aligned wins on both BREEDS subpopulation-shift splits (super13 +0.201, super26 +0.115, p_positive=1.00; runs/M8_ood/results.json), matching the paper's BREEDS robustness direction. However the non-reproduction of the utility half is entangled with the run's own recipe-fidelity gaps (substitute datasets, simplified aggressive KD) rather than a clean demonstration that the paper is wrong, and the disclosed reason (adaptation-scope trade-off) is plausible but not conclusively separable from under-faithful reproduction. Honest, partial agreement (OOD-BREEDS) with a disclosed but incompletely-attributable divergence on downstream utility.
